Disclaimer: I received my DK2 only one hour ago, and I've only tried the calibration scene & Tuscany.

So after an agonising wait today my DK2 finally turned up. I followed the setup procedure in the booklet and everything worked first time - though I'm sure that won't necessarily be the case when I start trying 3rd party experiences.

With a trembling hand I booted up the calibration scene. Tentatively, I slid the headset over my eyes - and promptly broke out in a huge grin, followed quickly by (I imagine) a slack-jawed expression of wonder. I'll be damned... They've done it! I thought.

Having read a lot (too much) about screen-door, black-smearing etc. I honestly expected to be disappointed. I wasn't. The amazing stereoscopic 3D blew all that away. I barely noticed a thing. I was too busy just moving my head around, examining the shapes of the card tower and plant in front of me. The shadows, the shading... I reach out my hand, and my stomach rewards me with the tiniest of flips when it's not there. Not nausea, just... an odd feeling.

I never tried the DK1, but I can't imagine this without positional tracking. I can move my head closer, even crane around the objects. It allows me to get a wonderful sense of their shape.

I realise I've been looking at an ordinary desk for about 15 minutes. Time to try Tuscany.

I load it up, and again, that wonderful sense of space. I don't move for a while, getting a sense of the room. The scale is the best part. Looking up at the rafters of the roof, my brain effortlessly understands the size of this space, and my size within it. I completely forget to check for black smearing, I'm having too much fun. In fact I didn't notice it at all during this session - although I intended to go in with a critical eye, that's all forgotten now.

I decided to start moving, and again that little flip of the stomach. Nothing big, just a little disconcerting. I start to worry about nausea. I get pretty sick when reading in the car, so I wonder if I'm susceptible to it. I keep moving slowly and deliberately, and I soon find I've acclimatised to the movement. I try the stairs. Here my body gives a slightly larger yelp as I go up. But I soon realise I'm not getting nauseous. It feels like it could potentially develop into that if I was playing some crazy parkour game or something, but here it just feels a little unusual, that's all. My biggest worry about using VR allayed.

I start to inspect the area, and find that the scene is fairly low quality. For example, it's totally obvious where a texture is "doing all the work". The shutters and cypress trees look particularly bad, obviously simple shapes with flat images pasted onto them.

I start to look more closely at the screen door effect. Sure, it's there, but it's nothing like as bad as I feared. As soon as I stop looking at it my brain seems to filter it out.

In the end I wander around Tuscany for about 35 minutes. No nausea.

All in all, my first experience has been overwhelmingly positive. Having read what seems like every thread and every comment on this subreddit, I actually went in with fairly negative expectations, planning to look for screen-door etc. To my surprise, all that melted away on first entering the VR world. My cynical nerdy impulses were beaten by childlike wonder.

I'm sure over time the defects of DK2 will start to bug me more. But for now I'm genuinely impressed (and surprised) that the experience actually matched up to the revelatory moment I'd dreamed of.
